Affordable skincare that’s absolutely NOT worth it vs the ones that 100% are. Part 1: the basics 

Absolutely not worth it ❌
Neutrogena Clear & Radiant Face Wash
Boots HABI Cleanse Away Cleansing Balm
Garnier Vitamin C Fresh & Bright Sorbet Cream
Garnier Hyaluron+ Barrier Repair Replumping Serum

Absolutely 100% worth it ✅
Geek & Gorgeous Jelly Joker, a low pH gentle cleanser that won’t strip your skin
B. Cleanse Melting Cleansing Balm from Superdrug
Illiyoon Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream, made for sensitive and dry skin
BYOMA Hydrating Serum with ceramides, squalane and glycerin

You don’t need to spend a fortune for good skin, you just need to know which ones are worth your money.

This is part 1 of a new series and there’s plenty more to come. Follow so you don’t miss part 2.

Save this for your next Boots or Superdrug trip.

Meg xx

#affordableskincare #skincaretips #budgetskincare

Where to actually save your money on skincare.

Not everything in your routine needs to be expensive. Your cleanser is on your face for 60 seconds. A hydrating eye cream is doing your moisturiser’s job. Hyaluronic acid is already in most of your products. And that new trending ingredient? If your skin is happy, you don’t need it.

Save here so you can spend where it actually counts. Part 2 is coming, where I’d actually spend my money.

Honest advice from a qualified skin specialist with 6 years in the industry.

meg x

#affordableskincare #skincaretips #skinspecialist

save your money, your hands do the job

slow and steady wins with actives

if it isn’t broken, don’t fix it

#ad @niod x @cultbeauty 

Copper peptides are a messenger. GHK-Cu carries the instruction that tells your skin cells to start repairing, and that’s the process behind your natural collagen production. It’s already in your body, and levels drop as you get older.

Copper Amino Isolate Serum (CAIS 3) from NIOD puts it back. 1% GHK-Cu copper peptide with 1% GHK peptide, watery, ultra lightweight, morning and night as your first step after cleansing.

In clinical testing on 31 people using it twice a day, it visibly repaired multiple types of wrinkles in 8 weeks.

The longer you use it, the more radiant and resilient your skin gets.

Shop it at Cult Beauty, link in my stories.

meg x

#NIOD #CultBeauty #copperpeptides

£50. One Boots. A full hydrating routine in 60 seconds. Did I do it? 👀

Here’s what went in the basket:
• Simple Repair Cleanser. I love a cleanser that leaves your skin feeling calm, not tight
• Boots Ingredients Ectoin. Honestly one of my favourite ingredients for dehydrated skin right now
• Q+A Collagen Face Cream. Lovely and comforting, perfect for sealing everything in
• Beauty of Joseon SPF. You all know I’ll never skip SPF, even on a budget

You really don’t need to spend a fortune to get your skin feeling hydrated and happy. Save this for your next Boots trip. Thanks for filming big dog @the_skinspecialist 

Meg x

#skincareonabudget #bootsskincare #hydratingskincare #dehydratedskin #skincareroutine affordableskincare
Kinda cringe until it isn’t 🥹 100k of you. I nearly didn’t post half the things that got me here, so this is your sign to post that damn post sat in your drafts!!! Thank you all so much, Meg x

@superdrug skincare alternatives that actually work, from a qualified skin specialist. Part 4 of my don’t buy this, buy this instead series. Save this before your next Superdrug trip huns, I got you x 

Peel swap in Superdrug. The Ordinary AHA 30% + BHA 2% Peeling Solution £8.90 (30ml) → Me+ AHA BHA Peel £7.50 (30ml). A third of the AHA, all of the glow.

Hydrating serum swap in Superdrug. SkinCeuticals Hydrating B5 £85 (30ml) → Superdrug Optimum Peptide Serum £15 (40ml). £70 back in your pocket.

Body swap in Superdrug. Naturium The Smoother Glycolic Acid Exfoliating Body Wash £19 (500ml) → Me+ Salicylic Acid & AHA Body Serum £8 (250ml). Acids that stay on your skin, not in the drain.

Vitamin C swap in Superdrug. Drunk Elephant C-Firma Fresh Day Serum £71 (28ml) → Geek & Gorgeous C-Glow £11.99 (30ml). Same key trio, £59 back.

PDRN swap in Superdrug. Lancôme Absolue Longevity The Soft Cream £140 (30ml) → VT PDRN Cream 100 £36 (50ml). The PDRN glow without the PDRN price.

Boots done, Superdrug done, plenty more shops to go. Follow so you don’t miss the next one, and tell me which shop you want me to raid next x

Stop making your own toner pads. It’s all over my fyp and it makes no sense.

Your toner was safety tested in its own bottle with its own lid. An open jar of damp cotton wool with your fingers in it every night is not that. That’s where bacteria grows.

You can buy sealed, properly preserved exfoliating toner pads in @bootsuk for around eight pounds. Or just put your toner on a cotton pad like you already do.

Save this before your next Boots trip.

meg x

#skincarehacks #exfoliatingtoner #tonerpads

I’m 36 and this is the affordable skincare I buy from the high street that proves it doesn’t have to be expensive to actually work.

Every one of these has earned its place in my routine, and in my opinion they outperform the expensive versions I’ve used. Cleanser, balm, peptide serum, moisturiser and retinoid, all without spending a fortune.

Hook inspo @bambidoesbeauty 

meg x
#affordableskincare #highstreetskincare #skincareover30

The viral Elemis dupe that keeps selling out at M&S. Same smell, same melt, and I think it outperforms it.

Remember the REN Evercalm balm? This performs just as well. Rich, thick, and a lifesaver for dry, irritated winter skin.

£9.99 and it beats every expensive moisturiser I’ve tried. You’ve seen it on my stories a hundred times for a reason.

Copper peptides, PDRN and ceramides for around £22. Peptide serums usually cost a fortune. This holds its own.

Does what retinoid serums three times the price do, with less irritation. The Ordinary just nail affordable skincare.

You don’t need to spend a lot on skincare. You need the right formulas, and they’re out there. Follow me for more. meg x

Two viral skincare products we’d never recommend as skin specialists 👀

Sophie’s is the SA Smoothing Cleanser. Salicylic acid in something you wash off isn’t doing much in 20 seconds, but it’s plenty long enough to leave her barrier feeling stripped. If you want that ingredient working properly it needs to be in something you leave on.

Mine is the Hydrating Cleanser. It feels like washing my face with conditioner. It just sits there. It’s not going to shift SPF or makeup on its own, and most people are using it as their only cleanse.

What do you guys think? A fan or both, none ?! Let us know ! 

Xx

Part 3 of Hills I’ll Die on (I mean not literally but I do believe these things whole heartedly) as a Dermatologist and Mom:

Bleach baths as recommended by your dermatologist can be a really great treatment adjunct for children and adults with eczema. The amount of plain 6% bleach will vary based off how much water is in a bathtub and if this preparation is for an adult or young child. Always consult with your provider first.

Studies have shown that non-sedating antihistamines can be a nice complement to use of isotretinoin and help alleviate some of the side effects. Omega-3 fish oil can also help with dryness while on the medication.

I have seen many people on the internet recommending the use of Hibiclens as a body wash. Let me be super clear - this should NOT be used as an every day body wash. Surgeons often recommend using it as a pre-op wash, but there are risks with eye and ear toxicity. 

Finally, if cosmetic procedures are on your list for this fall/winter, be sure you discuss with your dermatologist or provider regarding oral antiviral medications, particularly if you are prone to cold sores. And be sure to use your spf after!

Questions? Leave them below. This is not intended to be medical advice, this is for educational purposes only.

Wow @abbeyyung with the most beautiful hair!! 

It is truly so important whose advice you listen to when it comes to your health and in this case, your scalp and hair health. Hair loss is so much more than a simple “alopecia” diagnosis and comes with a myriad of many myths and sources of misinformation. One of those myths is that if you wash your hair more frequently this can cause more rapid hair loss. And I’m here to tell you that is simply not how it works. You notice more hair loss in the shower because loose hairs, or hairs in the shedding phase get washed out. 
It is not unusual to lose 100-150 hairs a day. Washing your scalp can actually lead to scalp build up and inflammation which can damage your hair. 

If you have significant hair loss or are losing hair in other parts of your body like eyebrows or eyelashes, seek out a board certified dermatologist for proper evaluation and management because hair loss is way more nuanced than you think.

As always, leave your questions below!

Beautiful skin on this creator- the azelaic acid + tretinoin combo is proving elite! But is it right for everyone?

So it depends. Tretinoin has years of data to support how it is truly the topical that will give you meaningful improvement in texture, acne, clarity, and collagen in your skin long term. 

Azelaic acid is great for those with sensitive skin or rosacea prone skin because it can help with inflammation, pigmentation as well as acne. It’s also good to use in pregnancy when other topicals are a no-go. But does azelaic help with anti oxidative support and collagen production? Not really.

Unless you use it for a specific reason, I would still say the best glass skin regimen includes a morning vitamin C and a nighttime retinoid that you can tolerate topically. Once you master the basics then you can add an additional active one at a time!

Leave your questions below!

#azelaicacid #tretinoin #glassskinroutine #glycolicacid #skintexture

I had so many questions regarding glycolic acid: what to use, when to use, what to do if you couldn’t tolerate it. Hopefully this breakdown gives more clarity. While I can’t give personalized medical advice, what I can tell you is the basic routine is truly the core for an effective skincare routine. Specific products would be tailored based on your skin type (oily, dry, combo).

Once you can consistently use your retinol or tretinoin nightly without irritation, it’s only then that I recommend adding more to your routine (if at all). Remember the core products stay the same.
This is where incorporating one active at a time is best. If you want to target pigmentation on your skin then azelaic acid is a good option. If it’s a thicker consistency and your vit c is a serum, then use your antioxidant first. Apply based on thinnest to thickest consistency. 
Then at bedtime swap out 2 nights out of the week to apply your AHA which serves as a chemical exfoliant. You could also talk to your dermatologist about increasing tretinoin strength instead of adding an AHA. Consistency of a tretinoin you tolerate is more important to me than the strength.

Finally, if you don’t find multiple steps too complicated and are happy with what you are wanting to improve (this will vary widely if you are acne prone, have hyperpigmentation etc). This is when you could add a peptide serum, growth factors etc to be the cherry on the cake!

Hopefully this gives you more clarity. Always talk to your dermatologist when starting products to determine what would be right for you. 

#glycolicacid #glassskinroutine #azelaicacid #tretinoin #retinolskincare

Tis the season for hand eczema! I see a big uptick of itchy hands when the seasons change. Frequent hand washing, stress, use of harsh soaps or hand sanitizers can all contribute to hand eczema. You may even see little “tapioca balls” on the sides of your fingers which are itchy water blisters. 

My best recommendation is to wash hands with lukewarm water and gentle fragrance free soap (this is where I would skip the dial soap). Moisturizer your hands liberally with a thick emollient (let me know if you want recs!) to protect your skin barrier.

If conservative measures don’t work, it’s time to see your local dermatologist for short term topical prescriptions if warranted!

As a dermatologist for close to a decade, I carefully and thoughtfully consider cosmetic procedures based off my experiences, my colleague’s experiences, how long a device and procedure has been on the market, what is the downtime, and who could benefit from this treatment? No cosmetic treatment is cheap and you should make an informed decision based on what may be best for YOU. 

Do I think biostimulatory fillers play a major role in regenerative medicine? Yes. Do I think they have their limitations? Yes. Do I think it impacts long term face lift procedure? No. However it does not give facelift results. I also do not recommend it if a patient plans to have a facelift within the next year or two.

Threads- no. There is a very slim patient population who I would say would benefit from this. I have seen more bad results from threads (misplacement, having to remove them, etc) than good. 

Microneedling- whether you are in your 20s, have more mature skin, or want to target acne scarring and pigmentation: a microneedling session is little downtime for big rewards. 

If you like this type of series let me know!
